en: Now, if you go to the official homepage and
then there to packages, you'll see a catalog
of available packages you can install and
you'll see the installation commands there
too
to extend Pi and add new capabilities to it.
And for example, here is already the first
extension I personally like having in my Pi
setup. Now again, you don't need any of
those and you should absolutely explore them
on your own too to see if there's anything
in here you wanna use. But Pi Web Access
simply extends the web access and web search
capabilities Pi has.
Now, it's worth noting that Pi out of the
box has web access capabilities because it
can use the Bash, the terminal,
and there it can use commands like curl to
send HTTP requests. So of course, Pi out of
the box can
download and view the content of websites.
Unless they block it.
But this extension here
expands these capabilities. And you can
always click on an extension to learn more
about it.
Pi Web Access simply adds more tools to Pi
that allow it to, for example, perform web
search through various providers, including
Gemini, so that Pi can use the Gemini API by
Google and the Gemini models behind the
scenes
to perform more powerful web search, web
search based on Google with summaries and
action by Gemini.
Now, that will cost you extra money though.
You'll be paying for the Gemini usage, but
in my experience, it's not super expensive,
just a couple of bucks every month for me,
and I'm using it a lot.
And it really makes web search way more
powerful and gives Pi
way more advanced web search capabilities.
But there also are other providers you could
configure and use to perform web search
through that extension. Again, not a
must-use, but something that can really be
useful.
Now it all starts with installing that
extension by running this command in your
command line. So not inside of Py, but
instead in your regular command line. And
this will install this extension globally on
your system.
And if you then run py list, you can see all
installed extensions. I got a couple of
other extensions here too,
including the DocParser extension, which is
an extension I created myself. You can also
find that in that packages registry. It's an
extension that helps with
reading PDF documents and other documents
through Pi, makes it a bit easier for Pi to
read those documents, but that's just a side
note.
But we'll get back to more extensions later.
So now I did install Pi Web Access, and even
without setting up a Gemini API key, this
already gives Pi some extra capabilities,
but it gets really powerful if you do
register an extra search provider, which can
be any of these, can be OpenAI, can be
Brave, which is a search provider, but in my
case, I prefer using Gemini. So you don't
need to configure all of them, just one of
them is enough to give Pi more advanced
search capabilities.
And you do that by adding a websearch.json
file
in your Pi folder, your global Pi folder. So
for me, that is the global Pi folder, and
then there, a websearch.json file. And then
if I open that file, there is a Gemini API
key, entry in there for me since I'm using
Gemini, and then my actual Gemini API key,
which I'm of course hiding here. So if using
Gemini for advanced search is also something
you want to do, what you'll have to do is go
to the Google Cloud Console, and you need a
Google Cloud account for that, of course, a
billing account. So that will cost you
money. That is really important to
understand.
And there under enabled APIs and services,
you'll need to make sure that the Gemini API
is enabled. And enable it if it's not.
And then under credentials,
you want to create a new API key. So create
credentials, API key for the Gemini
API. And for that, you need to check this
box here first so that you can select that.
And then select a service account or create
one if you don't have one yet. And then, for
example, restrict that key to only be usable
from your IP address.
Or apply no restrictions. And this will then
create an API key.
And you can then
copy that key. And I'll delete it after
recording that. So you don't need to bother
trying my key. And then set that in
websearch.json as a value for Gemini API
key.
And this is then all you need to do in order
to
enable Gemini-powered web search through
that Pi Web Access extension. Again, you
don't need to set this up. It has extra
capabilities even without doing that. But in
my experience, using Gemini for web search
really is a nice level up and gives Pi more
capabilities. But again, you'll be billed
per the Gemini API pricing. So that's
something to be aware of.
